source.authors: van Doan C, Züst T, Maurer C, Zhang X, Machado RAR, Mateo P, Ye M, Schimmel BCJ, Glauser G, Robert CAM
source.title: Herbivore-induced plant volatiles mediate defense regulation in maize leaves but not in maize roots

method: cross-exposure of intact receiver maize plants to herbivore-induced volatiles of leaves or roots of emitter plants, then caterpillar (S. littoralis) performance on receiver leaves
where: PMC copy of Plant Cell Environ 44(8): 2672-2686 (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8360093/), full article text opened, Section 3.5 (cross-exposure) and the abstract; the page prints that it is an open access article under the terms of the CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 License; DOI, volume, issue and pages checked on Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.1111/pce.14052, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)
value: receiver maize leaves exposed to volatiles from herbivore-infested leaves were followed by decreased performance of Spodoptera littoralis caterpillars; exposure to root volatiles did not have this effect
conditions: maize var. Delprim (one cultivar; the paper writes of maize generally); receiver plants exposed overnight, 17 h (5 p.m. to 10 a.m.), to emitter plants with leaf or root herbivory, in an 'unrealistic cross-exposure experiment' as the paper calls it; n = 4-5 per treatment (Figure 5 legend); the text gives no P value or effect size for panel a (it points to Table S7, not read). Not tested here: other maize genotypes, field conditions, exposure of receivers to individual compounds. The paper's root results are filed as the paired root record: root exposure to either leaf or root volatiles did not change root herbivore performance, and the abstract says HIPV exposure did not increase any measured root trait.
quote: Leaf exposure to leaf HIPVs, but not to root HIPVs, leads to a decreased performance of S. littoralis caterpillars (Figure 5a).
note: Full text read; the sentence is 20 words, ends with the figure reference as printed, and was seen whole on two fetches (127 characters). Abstract: 'Together, these results demonstrate that volatile-mediated defense regulation is restricted to the leaves of maize.' source.authors: van Doan C, Züst T, Maurer C, Zhang X, Machado RAR, Mateo P, Ye M, Schimmel BCJ, Glauser G, Robert CAM
source.title: Herbivore-induced plant volatiles mediate defense regulation in maize leaves but not in maize roots

method: cross-exposure of intact receiver maize plants to herbivore-induced volatiles of leaves or roots of emitter plants, then root herbivore (D. balteata) performance on receiver roots
where: PMC copy of Plant Cell Environ 44(8): 2672-2686 (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8360093/), full article text opened, Section 3.5 (cross-exposure) and the abstract; the page prints that it is an open access article under the terms of the CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 License; DOI, volume, issue and pages checked on Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.1111/pce.14052, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0)
value: no effect: root exposure to either leaf or root herbivore-induced volatiles before infestation did not change root herbivore (Diabrotica balteata) performance on maize
conditions: maize var. Delprim (one cultivar; the paper writes of maize generally); receiver plants exposed overnight, 17 h (5 p.m. to 10 a.m.), to emitter plants with leaf or root herbivory, in an 'unrealistic cross-exposure experiment' as the paper calls it; n = 4-5 per treatment (Figure 5 legend); the text gives no P value or effect size for panel a (it points to Table S7, not read). Not tested here: other maize genotypes, field conditions, exposure of receivers to individual compounds. Contrast: in the same experiment leaf exposure to leaf volatiles was followed by decreased S. littoralis performance on leaves (paired leaf record). The abstract adds that HIPV exposure did not reduce D. balteata performance or survival on maize or its ancestor teosinte, and did not increase constitutive or induced levels of any measured root trait.
quote: Root exposure to either leaf or root HIPVs prior infestation did not affect the root herbivore performance (Figure 5b).
note: Full text read; whole Results sentence (19 words) seen on two fetches, with the abstract's root-null sentences. A null result; the paper reads it as roots being impaired in emission and perception of resistance-inducing volatiles, which the cross-exposure design here does not separate from other causes. source.authors: Waterman JM, Cofer TM, Wang L, Glauser G, Erb M
source.title: High-resolution kinetics of herbivore-induced plant volatile transfer reveal clocked response patterns in neighboring plants

method: receiver maize plants exposed to volatiles of Spodoptera exigua-infested sender plants; receiver leaf gene expression sampled at 3, 8, 16.75 and 22 h of exposure, new plants per time point (Welch t-tests, Table 1)
where: version of record of eLife 12: RP89855 read as the PDF at elifesciences.org/articles/89855.pdf, results text, Table 1 and Figure 2 caption; Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.7554/eLife.89855) gives CC BY 4.0, volume 12, issued 2024-02-22
value: terpene biosynthesis genes (FPPS3, TPS2, TPS10, CYP92C5) in receiver maize leaves were induced by exposure to herbivore-induced volatiles during the day and not during the night, as the paper states; the per-time-point tests are mixed (see conditions)
conditions: inbred B73, V2 stage; senders carried three fourth-instar S. exigua larvae, control senders undamaged; gene expression n = 4-6 per time point. Table 1 p values (exposed against control): FPPS3 0.05 (3 h), 0.03 (8 h), 0.44 (16.75 h), 0.78 (22 h); TPS2 0.05, 0.09, 0.55, 0.07; TPS10 0.05, 0.12, 0.25, 0.02; CYP92C5 0.01, 0.30, 0.11, 0.22. So only FPPS3 is below 0.05 at 8 h, CYP92C5 only at 3 h, TPS2 at no time point (0.05 at 3 h), and TPS10 is also induced at 22 h (the beginning of the second day). The 3 and 8 h samples fall in the day and 16.75 h at night by the paper's wording, as read here; clock times are not printed. This is a receiver-leaf gene-induction timing result, not scent or flower timing. The paper does not test other genotypes, species or field conditions, nor ecological outcomes.
quote: All genes were induced by HIPV exposure during daytime, but not during the night.
note: Full text of the version of record read as PDF (the HTML page would not load); sentence seen whole on three fetches. Crossref gives volume 12, article RP89855, issued 22 February 2024, no issue, CC BY 4.0. Sentence following in the text: 'FPPS3 was slightly induced after 3 hr and significantly induced after 8 hr of HIPV exposure (Figure 2E, Table 1).' Reported as sense_chemical, not diel, per the owner's reading. POWO powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:426810-1 (opened) Zea mays L. source.authors: Yamauchi Y, Kunishima M, Mizutani M, Sugimoto Y
source.title: Reactive short-chain leaf volatiles act as powerful inducers of abiotic stress-related gene expression

method: intact plants exposed to vaporized volatile in a closed box; HSFA2 transcript measured over 0 to 2 h (qRT-PCR, Figure 1c)
where: PMC copy of Sci Rep 5: 8030 (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4306126/), full article text opened; the page prints 'licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 4.0 International License'; DOI, volume, issue and article number checked on Crossref
value: vaporized (E)-2-hexenal induced expression of the heat-shock factor gene HSFA2 within 30 min; the induction was transient and ended after 2 h; (E)-2-hexenol, (Z)-3-hexenal and n-hexanal did not induce HSFA2
conditions: Col-0, grown at 23 C on a 14 h light/10 h dark cycle; plant age at exposure not stated; (E)-2-hexenal at 10 nmol cm-3 (3 microlitres on paper in a 340 cm3 box) for 30 min, induction starting above about 2.5 nmol cm-3 and saturating near 25 nmol cm-3; n = 3 for HSFA2 induction. A leaf green-volatile at a high dose, not a herbivore-induced airborne signal from a neighbour; the paper does not identify how the volatile is perceived and does not test field conditions or other time points beyond 2 h.
quote: Vaporized (E)-2-hexenal rapidly and powerfully induced HSFA2 expression within 30 min (Fig. 1c).
note: Full text read; sentence (13 words) seen whole on two fetches, next sentence 'This expression was transient and terminated after 2 h.' Crossref: Scientific Reports volume 5, issue 1, article 8030, 26 January 2015, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. POWO powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:277970-1 (opened) Arabidopsis thaliana (L.) source.authors: Muroi A, Ramadan A, Nishihara M, Yamamoto M, Ozawa R, Takabayashi J, Arimura G
source.title: The Composite Effect of Transgenic Plant Volatiles for Acquired Immunity to Herbivory Caused by Inter-Plant Communications

method: greenhouse: intact receiver lima bean plants placed 30 or 60 cm from transgenic tobacco emitters overexpressing lima bean (E)-beta-ocimene synthase (NtOS2) for 7 days, then Tetranychus urticae infestation; volatile emission and Phytoseiulus persimilis olfactometer choice
where: full article page journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0024594 opened (abstract, Results, Discussion); volume, issue and article number checked on Crossref
value: priming of indirect defence was not detected in receiver lima bean plants placed 60 cm from the volatile-emitting transgenic tobacco, whereas receivers at 30 cm emitted more TMTT and methyl salicylate and attracted more predatory mites after spider-mite attack
conditions: lima bean cv. Pole Sieva (one cultivar; the abstract speaks of lima bean plants); emitters Nicotiana tabacum cv. SR1 line NtOS2 against wild-type tobacco; exposure 7 days in the greenhouse; olfactometer 70-80 predators over 3-4 replications; the 60 cm test gives no quantitative statistics in the text, only that priming was not detected. Other nulls: no oviposition difference between receivers of NtOS2 and wild-type emitters in the greenhouse; second-receiver mite attraction after 7 days P = 0.22; (E)-beta-ocimene emission just after exposure P = 0.27. The Discussion says the defence was exhibited only within 30 cm. Not tested: field conditions (transgenic plants), distances other than 30 and 60 cm in the greenhouse, direct-defence gene expression. The emitter is a transgenic tobacco, not a neighbouring lima bean.
quote: When VOCos-receiver plants were placed 60 cm apart, the priming of indirect defenses was not detected.
note: Full text read; Results sentence (15 words) seen whole on three fetches. The page text did not print a licence line; Crossref lists CC BY 4.0 for the PLoS ONE article (issued 12 October 2011, volume 6, issue 10, e24594).
